messages:
infra-alert: [ALERT] NV driver XID spikes detected on inference-west-2 pool. Nodes reporting repeated Xid 13/31/63 and correctable ECC increases: inf-gpu-13-04, inf-gpu-13-07, inf-gpu-13-12. Auto-evac initiated for 3 hosts. Link: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/2755554321 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm taking this — paging oncall. tagging @oncall-bot and @sre-lead. Can someone confirm customer-visible errors?

raj: seeing increased 500s in the API router logs from routes using ashburn cluster. Rough numbers: 1.7k QPS total, error rate up from 0.3% -> 4.9% on generation endpoints for that pool.

tony: NV kernel logs from inf-gpu-13-04 attached, looks like repeated nv-host-reset/Xid messages then container OOMs:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (139, 0) at 0x00000000
[ 12345.679101] nvidia-modeset: loading kernel module...
[ 12346.002234] containerd: runtime: killing container due to OOM
[ 12346.002245] kubelet: Evicting pod model-serving-abc on node inf-gpu-13-04
```

oncall-bot: Escalation: sev2 (customer impact >5% in region). Notifying customer-bridge-bot.

maria: OK sev2. Priority actions: 1) stop routing new inference to the affected pool, 2) force cordon + drain nodes if not already, 3) confirm if kernel driver restart helps, 4) open customer bridge if impact confirmed.

sam: Running cordon/drain now: ``kubectl cordon inf-gpu-13-04`` then ``kubectl drain inf-gpu-13-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60``. Doing inf-gpu-13-07 next.

kevin: On the runtime side, we launched automated fallback per routing policy: routes in group "inference-west-2" are failing over to "inference-west-2-bak" (smaller models + CPU fallback) — latency will increase. Notifying product that some customers will see higher tail latency.

abby: quick check on hardware telemetry: mem correctable errors spiked ~200/min on 13-04, 130/min on 13-07, 20/min on 13-12. 13-04 shows intermittent uncorrectable counts too (small). Possible early sign of failing DIMM or GPU memory bank.

maria: good context. @sre-lead any preference for driver restart vs node replacement? Reboots are disruptive.

sre-lead: If uncorrectable counts present, prefer replacement after draining. For correctable-only with transient Xid pattern, try driver unload/load and nv-host-reset first, with close monitoring for recurrence (15 min). If recurs escalate to replace.

raj: I ran `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.errors.uncorrected,memory.errors.corrected --format=csv` on 13-04: shows 26 uncorrected, 820 corrected.

tony: I can attempt `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` + `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` on inf-gpu-13-04 after we drain completed. Will coordinate maintenance window 2-3min.

maria: proceed after confirmation that no pods remain on node. @sam ping when drain done.

sam: drain finished for 13-04. No pods remaining. Starting driver unload now.

tony: driver unload/load done. Logs immediately show fewer Xid messages but telemetry still trending. Keeping under watch.

kevin: routing remains on fallback; error rate dropped from 4.9% -> 1.1% in last 6 mins. Latency for fallback routes increased p50 ~ +40ms, p95 +220ms.

customer-bridge-bot: Opening bridge for affected customers: acme-pay, citychat, notes.ai. Bridge link: https://bridge.internal/2755554321

abby: 13-07 drain in progress. 13-12 shows low uncorrectable counts; will hold and monitor for 30 min before evict.

maria: summary for the bridge: cause = driver/Xid + ECC correctable surge, impact = ~5% global errors for that pool (affecting 3 named customers), mitigation = forced routing fallback + node drains + driver reloads, next steps = replace nodes with flagged hardware if Xid reappears.

sre-lead: assign action items: sam - follow up on replacement convo with hw team, raj - collect full nv logs and attach to incident, tony - document exact driver commands and timings in the postmortem, abby - run extended ECC health scan on the rack, kevin - monitor routing and rollback if errors resurface.

sam: noted. I filed a replacement ticket to hw-provisioning: ticket #HW-84219 referencing nodes inf-gpu-13-04/07, requested expedited replacement and DIMM checks.

raj: attached nv logs + system dmesg to the incident ticket. snippet: ```
NVRM: Xid (31, 0x0a) at GPU 0000:65:00.0: pid 23345: kernel:187
NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

maria: any confirmed customer error rates in bridge? @customer-bridge-bot

customer-bridge-bot: customers on bridge reporting timeouts for heavy-generation requests; some have fallback to smaller models but not all. acme-pay reports 12% of requests errored for a 20-min window. Bridge established, planned updates every 15 min.

tony: for completeness, here's the quick mitigation steps run:
```
kubectl cordon inf-gpu-13-04
kubectl drain inf-gpu-13-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
sudo systemctl stop model-serving
sudo modprobe -r nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo systemctl start model-serving
```

maria: timeline note: driver reload at +8m reduced spikes temporarily, but 13-07 showed recurrence after 12m -> we are replacing 13-07. 13-12 remains under watch. Marking incident with action: hardware replacement for nodes with persistent Xid patterns.

sre-lead: keep oncall handoff at 2-hourly cadence until fully resolved. Postmortem owner: tony. Severity will remain sev2 until all replacements done and error rate <0.5% for 3x 30-min windows.

raj: adding tiny follow-up: check if kernel patch landed in last deploy for GPU driver module versions. Might correlate.

maria: thanks team. Next update in 15. If anything spikes, ping with :rotating_light:.

oncall-bot: handoff scheduled to next oncall in 1h 50m.

kevin: monitoring alert: error rate holding ~0.9% after current mitigations. Continuing to watch routing and capacity.

maria: closing initial paging loop — will stay in bridge for customer updates. Postmortem draft to follow after hardware replacement and logs fully collected.

customer-bridge-bot: final note to bridge: we will provide RCA and timeline once HW replacement and full root-cause analysis complete.
